method: Input is read in the browser and nothing is executed, stored or sent. A leading angle-bracket priority is taken from the start of the text, so both an RFC 5424 line such as <134>1 2026-11-09T05:00:00Z host app - - - started and an older BSD line such as <34>Nov 9 05:00:00 host app: started decode from the same token; the rest of the line is ignored. A bare run of digits is read as a priority, a value with a leading zero is refused because RFC 5424 writes the priority without padding, and anything outside 0 to 191 is refused with the range in the message. A pair is split on a single dot: the facility part is matched case-insensitively against the 24 RFC 5424 facility keywords (kern to local7, with kernel as an alias for kern and a numeric 0 to 23 also accepted), and the severity part against the eight keywords emerg to debug, also accepting panic or emergency for emerg, critical for crit, error for err, warn for warning and informational for info, or a numeric 0 to 7. The priority is facility times 8 plus severity, and the result reports the facility code and description, the severity code, keyword, name and meaning, the equivalent journalctl --priority keyword, and the arithmetic that produced the number. The severity and facility tables below the form are rendered from the same data, and each common-priority shortcut decodes a pair through the same path.
